top_categories.workout_context: 273 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
Karukinka's Chilean Tierra del Fuego, South American gravel forces constant power changes. Surge over the rough stuff, settle on the smooth, repeat for 273 miles.
At Karukinka, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
18,045ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
66ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Karukinka's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before February.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 273 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
273 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Karukinka. Train it until it feels boring.
18,045ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Karukinka, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 18,045ft of climbing on tierra del Fuego mountain gravel does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 273 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 273 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.terrain: Highly technical terrain at Karukinka demands practice on similar surfaces. Ride tierra del fuego mountain gravel at race-day cadence weekly. Expect: chilean tierra del fuego, south american gravel, regional event. Practice cornering, descending, and power delivery on unstable surfaces. Dial in tire pressure before race week — 5 PSI wrong costs you 15+ minutes over 273 miles.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Gravel Specific, and Over Under to prepare you for 273 miles of tierra del fuego mountain gravel in Tierra del Fuego, Chile.
